title: SLO‑orchestrated evacuation simulator and restore fidelity harness
creator: Asha Patel
description: Build a lightweight, repeatable simulator and validation harness that executes SLO-driven active->passive evacuation scenarios against a staging copy of production. The goal is to (1) validate end-to-end restore fidelity for KV and tokenstore snapshots, (2) exercise circuit-breaker and load-shedding policies under progressive traffic degradation, and (3) measure SLO regressions and recovery time when promoting passive regions. This ticket scopes the harness, the drill templates, and automation to produce a quantitative restore-fidelity score and SLO regression report.
acceptance_criteria: Run a scheduled drill that simulates a passive-region promotion with at least three traffic cohorts (gold, standard, bulk) and capture per-cohort latency, error-rate, and token success metrics.
Restore fidelity >= 99.5% for KV lookups and tokenstore rehydration compared with production baseline fingerprints for 95% of test inputs.
Circuit-breaker policies automatically engage at configured thresholds and trigger progressive load-shedding actions; verify graceful degradation rules execute in correct order.
Automated rollback is exercised and validated: on failed restore-fidelity < 98% or catastrophic data mismatch, system reverts routing to origin region within defined SLO for rollback.
Produce a drill report in the Console with token-level cost delta, latency histogram, error-tag breakdown, and a restore-fidelity scorecard exported to Confluence and the incident dashboard.
tasks: Design simulator harness interface and CLI (owner: Ethan)
Implement snapshot fingerprint comparator for KV and tokenstore (owner: Priya Singh)
Integrate circuit-breaker emulator to drive progressive failures (owner: Miguel Lopez)
Create cohorted traffic generator with latency distributions and tail-noise injection (owner: Asha Patel)
Add telemetry exporters for Console: per-route SLO deltas, token cost, and restore-fidelity metrics (owner: Observability team)
Author drill templates and runbook for on-call and SRE (owner: Reliability PM)
Automate report generation and Confluence upload (owner: Solutions Eng)
Write e2e test harness and CI job that runs the simulator nightly against staging snapshots (owner: CI team)
progress_updates: 2026-02-12: Kickoff meeting with Reliability, Observability, and Infra. Agreed SLO thresholds: p95 latency increase <= 20%, error-rate spike <= 5x, rollback window 10 minutes.
2026-02-18: Prototype traffic cohort runner merged (PR #github.com/redwood/ci/pull/2143). Cohorts: gold(5%), standard(65%), bulk(30%).
2026-02-24: Snapshot fingerprint design completed. Chose combination of SHA256 keys + probabilistic bloom check for large blob sets to bound runtime.
2026-03-02: Circuit-breaker emulator added; initial run shows expected tiered shedding but revealed an ordering bug in routing fallback — assigned to Ethan for hotfix.

2026-03-08: First full drill run against staging snapshots. Observability captured KV mismatch rate 1.1% and token rehydration missing keys 0.7%. Investigating root causes for missing tokens in restore pipeline.
2026-03-12: Post-mortem notes added; plan to increase snapshot chunk granularity and retry-window in restore job. Updated acceptance thresholds to require additional verification step.
test_plan: Establish staging snapshots: take production-consistent KV and tokenstore snapshots at T0, tag with fingerprint metadata.
Run baseline collector against production for a set of 10k synthetic reads to create expected response vectors.
Execute simulator: spin up passive-region staging infra, restore snapshots, run cohorted traffic for 30 minutes with injected tail noise and backend error bursts.
Validate fingerprint comparator: compute diff report and fail criterion if mismatches over threshold or missing keys present.
Verify circuit-breaker behavior: trigger backpressure at 30%, 60%, and 90% of capacity and assert shedding order and recovery hysteresis.
Measure SLOs: capture p50/p95/p99 latency, error-rate, and token success; compare to baseline and flag regressions.
Run automated rollback scenario by flipping routing back to primary when restore-fidelity < 98% and validate rollback completion within 10 minutes.
rollback_plan: Immediate: Flip traffic back to primary region via routing control-plane (runbook step 3) and mark passive promotion as failed.
Confirm consistency: run a targeted validation to ensure no write divergence occurred during attempted promotion.
Remediate snapshots: abort incremental backfill jobs and re-run restore with increased chunk size and retry windows.
Post-rollback: create postmortem, schedule deeper DR run after fixes, and notify customer-facing teams if customer-impacting thresholds were reached.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Restores may expose latent bugs in incremental snapshot rotation leading to partial key loss. Mitigation: enforce pre-drill checksum and run small-sample rehydrate tests before cohort injection.

Risk: Circuit-breaker emulator could over-exercise synthetic failure modes not representative of real-world hardware issues. Mitigation: seed emulator with observed production failure profiles and validate against historical incidents.
Risk: Drill generates significant cost due to token replays. Mitigation: limit synthetic tokens and use cached prefix replay where applicable; report cost delta in drill summary.
Risk: False positives from fingerprint comparator due to timing differences. Mitigation: add configurable time-window tolerance and metadata-based gating before fail decisions.
notes: Decision: use fingerprint+probabilistic checks instead of full object compare to keep validation runtime under 10 minutes for large namespaces.
Tradeoff: stricter restore-fidelity threshold increases false negatives but reduces risk of silent data loss; we chose 99.5% target but will gate on 98% for automatic rollback.
Follow-up: add a canaryless promotion path for low-risk namespaces (metrics-only) to reduce customer impact during early-stage runs.
Action item: schedule cross-team tabletop for on-call, SRE, and product to practice runbook steps before first customer-facing drill.
